title: Terminal project
description: One way a run can END WELL (M5 task T87 · FR-STY-06 groundwork · GDD Part XVI "Legacy: the run resolves toward its ending — hold, escape, sacrifice, or fall"). Static, content-as-data definition of a staged undertaking the base builds. The engine (sim/project.ts) is a generic interpreter — no per-project branching: it offers a commit verb for each project at the player's own shelter, then the NEXT unfinished stage of whatever was committed to, debits ONE accepted payment, spends `timeCost` hours, applies the stage's `escalation`, and on the last stage sets `ending.escaped` or `ending.held` — which is the only thing `runEndReason` reads. Committing is EXCLUSIVE: one project per run, so the second is the road not taken. A stage is paid with ANY ONE entry of its `accepts` menu, never a bill of materials: measured (measure/t87.ts --ledger-immortal), the city hands an immortal 36-day run about 6 scrap and roughly ONE each of eight other things, so a conjunctive cost is unpayable while a disjunctive one is payable many ways — and that is what turns the items nothing ever wanted (batteries, lighter, blanket) into alternate payments rather than hard gates. Every stage RAISES something, because the whole point is that building toward the ending makes the city harder.

qty.description: Units of the item — a whole, positive count.

escalation.description: What finishing this stage does to the world, applied once, the moment it lands. On top of this one-shot the engine adds a STANDING lift to every region's drift anchor for each completed stage (PROJECT_ALARM_PER_STAGE), so the pressure does not decay away between stages.

survivorActivity.description: Rivals notice. Raising this also drains the region's loot faster (the T17 contest), so a loud project eats the city it is trying to leave.

scope.description: "region" (the shelter's own region — the default) or "city" (every region).

id.description: Stable slug, unique within the project. Part of the endingFlags key, so it is save data — never rename one.

worldEffect.description: What it does in the world, never a number ("The seams stop weeping. It will float.").

accepts.description: Accepted payments — ANY ONE settles the stage. Ordered: the engine takes the first the player can afford, so put the payment the stage would rather have first. Price these off the measured ledger, not off what the fiction suggests: an item that is never found is fine here as an ALTERNATE and fatal as the only entry.

timeCost.description: Hours the stage costs. > 0, so every stage is a resolved, world-advancing turn (FR-CORE-03).

noise.description: Deposited at the node by pipeline stage 6, exactly as a firearm or a molotov is.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint pointing at this schema.

id.description: Stable content id of the form project.<departure|holdout>.<slug>. It is part of every endingFlags key this project writes, so it is SAVE DATA — never rename a shipped project.

kind.description: Which ending finishing this project resolves to: "escape" sets ending.escaped, "holdout" sets ending.held.

label.description: The project's name, as the base would say it.

premise.description: The commit row's prose — what you are choosing, in the world's words, with no numbers in it.

stages.description: Ordered. A stage is offered only once every earlier one is done.

ending.description: The run's closing narration when the last stage lands. A scene, not a scoreboard (GDD IX rule 5).
